title: EU budget summit collapses in Brussels amid disputes and boycotts
seoTitle: EU budget summit collapses in Brussels amid disputes
dek: An extraordinary European Union summit in Brussels on 26 November collapsed after a group of nations walked out of negotiations over the 2028-2034 budget.
happened: On 26 November, leaders of the 27 European Union member states gathered in Brussels for an extraordinary summit convened by European Council President António Costa to discuss the 2028-2034 long-term budget. According to Euronews, the meeting was preceded by discussions on Christine Lagarde's succession at the European Central Bank. The budget talks quickly stalled due to deep divisions between member states favoring traditional spending such as agriculture and those demanding cuts to reallocate funds toward defense and security. António Costa proposed a compromise budget of €1.78 trillion, but met resistance from all sides. To bridge the gap, Costa organized breakout sessions in small groups, which frustrated several nations who viewed the format as an attempt to divide them. According to European Pravda and Politico, nations advocating for smaller budgets—including Denmark, Sweden, Belgium, Austria, Finland, Germany, and the Netherlands—boycotted further small-group negotiations. Consequently, European leaders abandoned the planned second day of talks, and António Costa shortened his closing press conference. Leaders now aim to resume negotiations at the upcoming summit in December.

sides.says: Several nations pushing for a smaller budget, including Denmark, Sweden, Belgium, Austria, Finland, Germany, and the Netherlands, boycotted small-group discussions. According to Politico, diplomats stated, "It was obvious this was a move to divide us, to buy each of us seven off with a gift. It just went really badly. It was not a real discussion."

European Council President António Costa defended the summit format, stating according to Euronews, "This meeting was a necessary step in the process. This is a negotiation process. It is normal that the different parties are starting to underline and mark their starting points. Everybody knows that we cannot fail Europe, and we need to have a new budget from the 1st of January 2028."

French President Emmanuel Macron criticized proposed budget cuts as a strategic mistake and warned that dragging negotiations past the new year is democratically impossible due to upcoming presidential elections in France, according to Politico and Euronews.

next: European Union leaders will attempt to reach an agreement on the multiannual financial framework during the upcoming summit scheduled for December.
summary: An extraordinary European Union summit in Brussels collapsed on 26 November after negotiations on the 2028-2034 long-term budget ran into fierce opposition. European Council President António Costa attempted to bridge gaps between opposing factions through small-group discussions. However, several countries demanding a smaller budget boycotted the format, leading leaders to cut the summit short by a day. Discussions are now expected to resume at a subsequent Brussels summit in December, amid warnings from leaders regarding electoral timelines.
